title: Repo skeleton
acceptance: docker compose up starts Postgres, the Go API and the mock provider
make verify passes
Every later slice has a fixed place for its spec, plan, decisions and progress

FR-6: the header shows the sidebar toggle, the page search and the light and dark toggle only

FR-8: the page search lists only the sidebar pages

NFR-2: pnpm lint passes

title: Seed users
acceptance: FR-1: seed applies all goose migrations before it inserts data.
FR-2: On an empty database, seed inserts SEED_USERS random users plus the edge-case users from goal.md.
FR-3: If users contains rows, seed makes no change and exits with code 0.
FR-4: With SEED_RESET=true, seed deletes all users and events, then inserts them again.
FR-5: The same SEED_RANDOM and seed time give the same rows.
FR-6: Each language is tr or en. Each country is TR or US. Check constraints reject other values. Each TR user is tr and each US user is en.
FR-7: Each email is unique and ends with @example.com.
FR-8: Each phone matches ^\+905\d{9}$ for TR or ^\+1\d{3}55501\d{2}$ for US.
FR-9: Each city is in the list for the user's country.
FR-10: The country, language and consent ratios are within 3 percentage points of the table in goal.md.
FR-11: For each user, the summary columns are equal to the values calculated from events.
FR-12: Each purchase event has an amount greater than 0. Each cart_add event has a null amount.
FR-13: The example brief's rule from goal.md, with language = tr, selects at least 1 user.
NFR-1: seed inserts 5,000 users in less than 10 seconds. Use pgx CopyFrom.
NFR-2: The migrations add indexes on users.city, users.language, users.last_cart_add_at, users.last_purchase_at and events.user_id.
NFR-3: docker-compose.yml has a seed service with restart: "no". api depends on it with condition: service_completed_successfully.
NFR-4: make up starts the stack on an empty volume. The users table then contains the seeded rows.
NFR-5: The generator is a pure function of the random seed and the seed time. Tests run it with no database.

NFR-6: Tests for FR-1 to FR-4 and FR-11 run against Postgres. They read TEST_DATABASE_URL. make test starts a temporary Postgres container and sets this variable. Without the variable, go test skips these tests.
NFR-7: make verify passes.
NFR-8: The seed binary imports nothing from internal/ except config, store and seed.

title: Mock SMS and email provider
acceptance: FR-1. POST /v1/sms and POST /v1/email with a valid body return 202 with a new id. The provider stores the message.

FR-2. A request that is not valid returns 400 with code: invalid_request. The provider stores nothing. This includes an SMS body over 160 characters, a subject over 80 characters, a bad to and a missing required field.
FR-3. The provider counts characters as runes. An SMS body of 160 Turkish characters, for example ş, gets 202. A body of 161 characters gets 400.
FR-4. A repeat request with the same body and reference gets 202 and a new id. The provider stores both. duplicate_deliveries goes up by 1.
FR-5. When a channel is over its rate limit, the provider returns 429 with a Retry-After header of 1 or more. A 429 on sms does not use an email token.
FR-6. With MOCK_RATE_PER_SEC=100 and the default burst, 200 requests sent at once to one channel get at least one 429. 100 requests sent at a steady 100 per second get no 429.
FR-7. X-Mock-Fail: 500 and X-Mock-Fail: 503 return that status. The provider stores nothing.
FR-8. X-Mock-Fail: slow returns 202 after MOCK_SLOW_DELAY. The provider stores the message.
FR-9. X-Mock-Fail: lost closes the connection with no response. The provider stores the message. The client gets a transport error, not an HTTP status.
FR-10. X-Mock-Fail: 429 returns 429 with Retry-After: 1 and uses no token. X-Mock-Fail: none gets no random failure. Any other value gets 400.
FR-11. With all three rates at 0, 1,000 valid requests get 202.
FR-12. With a fixed MOCK_RANDOM, the count of each failure mode over 10,000 requests is within 1 percentage point of its rate.
FR-13. GET /v1/messages filters by channel, to and reference. It sorts newest first and applies limit and offset. total counts all matches.
FR-14. GET /v1/stats gives each counter from goal.md for each channel. The counters match the responses that the provider sent.
FR-15. DELETE /v1/messages returns 204. After it, GET /v1/messages gives total: 0 and all counters are 0.
FR-16. An env var that is not valid stops the process at startup with a clear error. This includes a rate outside 0 to 1, a sum of rates over 1, and a bad duration.
NFR-1. The handlers are safe for concurrent requests. A test sends 500 requests from 50 goroutines. delivered is then equal to the count of 202 responses plus lost responses.
NFR-2. Tests use httptest and an injected clock and sleep function. No test waits for MOCK_SLOW_DELAY or for the rate limiter in real time.
NFR-3. Tests set the failure rates and do not depend on the defaults.
NFR-4. docker-compose.yml passes each MOCK_* env var to mock-provider, with the defaults from goal.md. .env.example lists them as comments.
NFR-5. make up starts mock-provider. curl -X POST localhost:8081/v1/sms with a valid body and X-Mock-Fail: none returns 202.
NFR-6. cmd/mockprovider imports nothing from internal/ except config and mockprovider. internal/mockprovider imports nothing from internal/.
NFR-7. make verify passes.

title: Segment rules
acceptance: FR-1. POST /api/segments/preview with the example brief and the default mock returns 200. The response has the rule, the description and an audience with email and sms of 1 or more.
FR-2. Sanitization removes control characters except \n and \t, format characters and <brief> tags, with case ignored. It normalizes to NFC and trims the text. A table test covers each step.

FR-3. A brief with no letter, or with more than 1,000 runes after sanitization, returns 400 with code: invalid_brief. The LLM client gets no call. A brief of 1,000 Turkish runes, for example ş, is valid.
FR-4. A body over 16 KiB, a body that is not valid JSON, or a body with no brief returns 400 with code: invalid_request.

FR-5. The validator rejects each case in "Validation". A table test has one or more cases for each item. The cases include an unknown field, an unknown operator, a wrong operator for a field, a string "30" for within_days, a city not on the list, between with low over high, an in list of 21 values, depth 4, 21 conditions, an unknown key and data after the object.
FR-6. The validator returns all errors with a path, not only the first.
FR-7. SQL injection in a value fails validation. Examples: "Istanbul' OR 1=1 --" for city, and "city; DROP TABLE users" as a field name.
FR-8. For each field and operator, the compiler gives the expected SQL text and parameters. No value from the rule is in the SQL text.
FR-9. With a fixed clock, within_days, older_than_days and age give the expected time and date parameters.
FR-10. An empty root group compiles to TRUE and counts all users. An empty nested group fails validation.

FR-11. If the first LLM answer fails validation and the second is valid, the response is 200. The second request to the mock contains the first answer as a tool call. It also contains the validation errors as a tool result with the error flag.
FR-12. If both LLM answers fail validation, the response is 422 with code: segment_invalid and the errors in details. The backend runs no count query.
FR-13. An unsupported answer returns 422 with code: segment_unsupported and the reason. The backend runs no count query.
FR-14. An ok answer with unmapped returns 200 with the unmapped list. More than 5 items, or an item over 200 runes, fails validation.

FR-15. Against Postgres, the audience counts are equal to the counts that a test calculates in Go from the seeded users. The test covers the example rule, an or group, an age between rule and an empty root.

FR-16. audience.languages has one entry for each language in the audience, sorted by reachable from high to low, then by code. A language with reachable of 0 is not in the list. A rule with country in [TR, US] gives two entries. The example rule gives only tr.
FR-17. A rule that selects no users returns 200 with all counts at 0 and an empty languages list.
FR-18. The same rule always gives the same description. Each field and each operator has a test.

FR-19. An LLM client error returns 502 with code: llm_error. A timeout returns 504 with code: llm_timeout. A refusal returns 502 with code: llm_refused and no repair round. The test uses the mock and an injected timeout, with no real wait.
FR-20. The system prompt contains each allowlist field, each operator and each city. A test builds the prompt and checks this.
FR-21. The user message puts the sanitized brief between <brief> and </brief>. The system prompt does not contain the brief.

FR-22. On /campaigns/new, the operator enters a brief and clicks "Find audience". The page shows "Generating segment…" while the request runs, then the description, the counts, the languages and the unmapped notes.
FR-23. On an API error, the page shows the API message and keeps the brief. The page shows unmapped and reason as text, not as HTML.

FR-24. For each user in the result of the recipients function for sms, sms_consent is true. The same is true for email. The test uses a rule that matches the seed users with no consent, and they are not in either result.
FR-25. no_consent is equal to matched minus reachable, in the top level and in each language entry.
FR-26. A first answer with no submit_segment call gets a repair round. The repair request ends with a user text message, not a tool result.
NFR-1. The compiler accepts only the validated rule type. No function in internal/segment takes raw JSON and returns SQL.

NFR-2. The allowlist is in one table. The validator, the compiler, the description, the prompt and the tool schema read it. A test adds a fake field to a copy of the table and checks that all five use it.
NFR-3. The count query has a 2 second statement timeout. A timeout returns 503 with code: db_unavailable.
NFR-4. Tests use the mock LLM. No test reads ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. With LLM_MODE=mock, the api starts with no key.
NFR-5. Logs contain no brief text and no API key.
NFR-6. internal/segment imports nothing from internal/. internal/llm imports nothing from internal/ except config.
NFR-7. The Postgres tests read TEST_DATABASE_URL, as in slice 02. Without it, go test skips them.
NFR-8. Frontend tests mock the API. pnpm test:run, pnpm build and CI=true pnpm lint pass.
NFR-9. make up with no .env starts the stack. The example brief on /campaigns/new shows an audience.
NFR-10. make verify passes.
NFR-11. The recipients function is the only function in internal/segment that returns user rows. Its channel argument is a type with two values. No argument turns off the consent condition.
